relationships.subject: NaV1.7
relationships.evidence_quote: Loss-of-function recessive mutations in NaV1.7 (also known as PN1) were found to cause Congenital insensitivity to pain (CIP) [60].

relationships.subject: NSAIDs
relationships.evidence_quote: NSAIDs exert their effects through inhibition of cyclooxygenase (COX-1 and COX-2), but this mechanism produces substantial off-target toxicity

key_findings: Review: NaV1.8 is a stronger analgesic target than NaV1.7, whose selective inhibitors failed clinically; suzetrigine (NaV1.8 inhibitor) was approved for acute pain.
NaV1.7, NaV1.8 and NaV1.9 act as an interdependent unit in DRG nociceptors, with NaV1.7 setting threshold and NaV1.8 driving the upstroke.
